title: Completion of flat algebra deformations and automatic adic completeness
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with ideal $J$. Let $\mathrm{Art}_k$ consist of Artinian local commutative $k$-algebras $A$ with specified residue field $k$ (Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize), and local $k$-maps respecting that field. Write $\mathfrak m_A$ for the maximal ideal. A marked flat deformation of $B$ over $A$ is a flat $A$-algebra $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] with a specified isomorphism $Q/\mathfrak m_AQ\cong B$, and arrows over $A$ are isomorphisms respecting it. Let $J_Q$ be the inverse image of $J$ under this quotient. Then $Q$ is Noetherian, and $\widehat Q=\varprojlim_n Q/J_Q^n$ is Noetherian, flat over $A$, and complete for $J_Q\widehat Q$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Its reduction is canonically $\widehat B$. Completion gives a functor of marked deformation groupoids, compatible with base change: for every map $A\to A_1$ in $\mathrm{Art}_k$ there is a natural marked isomorphism $\widehat Q\otimes_A A_1\cong\widehat{Q\otimes_A A_1}$, the latter completion taken along the inverse image of $J$. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Furthermore, if $B$ is already $J$-adically complete, every marked flat deformation $Q$ of $B$ is $J_Q$-adically complete. If also $B$ is local and $J$ is its maximal ideal, $Q$ is a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $J_Q$.

source.place: Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion), functor and proof; algebra.tex Tag 0DYC (lemma-complete-modulo-nilpotent) for automatic completeness. Finite-module completion gives the natural Artinian base-change isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $H=\mathfrak m_AQ$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], $\mathfrak m_A$ has finitely many generators and $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$. Their images generate $H$ and $H^N=0$. The inverse system $Q/H^n$ is constantly $Q$ for $n\ge N$, so its canonical limit map is an isomorphism. Since $Q/H=B$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] applied to $(Q,H)$ makes $Q$ Noetherian. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] to $(Q,J_Q)$ shows that $\widehat Q$ is Noetherian and complete for $J_Q\widehat Q$; $J_Q$ is finitely generated because $Q$ is Noetherian. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] makes $Q\to\widehat Q$ flat, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] composes it with the given flat map $A\to Q$.

source.place: Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion), proof, Noetherianity and flatness paragraphs; algebra.tex Tags 05GH, 0316, 05GG, 00MB.

proof.text: The $Q$-module $B=Q/H$ is cyclic and the image of $J_Q$ is $J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] with ring $Q$, ideal $J_Q$ and module $B$. It gives the canonical bijection $\widehat Q\otimes_Q B\cong\widehat B$, hence $\widehat Q\otimes_A k\cong\widehat B$: tensor associativity identifies both with $\widehat Q/H\widehat Q$. The completion comparison on a simple tensor is $u\otimes b\mapsto (u_n b\bmod J^n)_n$; this formula preserves products and units, so the bijection is an algebra isomorphism. This supplies the marking on $\widehat Q$.

source.place: Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion), final paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3).

proof.text: Every $C\in\mathrm{Art}_k$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] gives generators $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of $\mathfrak m_C$ and $\mathfrak m_C^N=0$. Every $c\in C$ is a scalar from $k$ plus $\sum_i t_i c_i$, by the specified residue-field isomorphism. Iterating this expression $N$ times writes $c$ as a $k$-linear combination of the finitely many monomials in the $t_i$ of total degree less than $N$. For any $A\to A_1$ in $\mathrm{Art}_k$, a finite $k$-spanning set of $A_1$ also spans it over $A$; hence $Q_1=Q\otimes_A A_1$ is finite as a $Q$-module. Its special fibre is $B$ by associativity and the residue markings. It is flat over $A_1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], so step 1 applies to $Q_1$.

source.place: Tag 0DYV, natural functor of deformation categories; finite-module hypothesis for algebra.tex Tag 00MA, expanded using the Artinian base.

proof.text: Let $L=J_QQ_1$, $H_1=\mathfrak m_{A_1}Q_1$, and let $K$ be the inverse image of $J$ in $Q_1$. The image of $L$ in $Q_1/H_1=B$ is $J$, whence $K=L+H_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], $H_1^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$. Expand a product of $n+N$ elements from $L+H_1$: each term either has at least $N$ factors from $H_1$ and vanishes, or at least $n$ factors from $L$. Thus $K^{n+N}\subseteq L^n\subseteq K^n$. The two completion limits are canonically isomorphic: one map uses $Q_1/L^n\to Q_1/K^n$, its inverse uses $Q_1/K^{n+N}\to Q_1/L^n$. Compatibility of sequences makes both composites identity at every quotient. This comparison is induced by the identity of $Q_1$.

source.place: Tag 0DYV, cartesian compatibility; cofinal ideal-power comparison required to use Tag 00MA after base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] to the finite $Q$-module $Q_1$. It gives $\widehat Q\otimes_A A_1=\widehat Q\otimes_Q Q_1\cong\varprojlim_n Q_1/L^n$. The formula at level $n$ is $u\otimes a_1\mapsto u_n\otimes a_1\bmod L^n$, which is multiplicative and unital. Compose with step 4 to obtain $\widehat Q\otimes_A A_1\cong\widehat{Q_1}_K$. For a marked isomorphism $f:Q\to Q'$, the quotient maps $f_n$ send $J_Q^n$ onto $J_{Q'}^n$, so $(x_n)\mapsto(f_n(x_n))$ defines its completion and preserves identities and composition coordinatewise. Naturality of the tensor comparison is included in the cited node. All comparisons commute with step 2's markings: reduction to $k$ gives the same displayed formula for $B$. For $A\to A_1\to A_2$, the successive and direct comparisons send $u\otimes a_1\otimes a_2$ at every finite quotient to $u_n\otimes(a_1a_2)$, using the image of $a_1$ in $A_2$. Equality on simple tensors gives the cocycle condition; identity base maps give identity comparisons. Thus completion gives the required functor and natural marked base-change isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion), natural functor, expanding Artinian base-change coherence using algebra.tex Tag 00MA.

proof.text: Assume $B$ is $J$-adically complete. The nilpotence in step 1 makes $Q$ complete for $H=\mathfrak m_AQ$. It is Noetherian by that step, and $Q/H=B$ is complete for the image $J$ of $J_Q$. Apply [lem-sfb-two-ideal-adic-completeness] with $R=Q$, $I=H$, and second ideal $J_Q$. This proves that the canonical map $Q\to\widehat Q$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DYC (lemma-complete-modulo-nilpotent), applied with nilpotent first ideal.

proof.text: If $B$ is local with maximal ideal $J$, the inverse image $J_Q$ is maximal, since $Q/J_Q=B/J$ is a field. Every $q\notin J_Q$ has unit image in $B$; lift its inverse to $r\in Q$. Then $qr=1+h$ for $h\in H$, and $(1+h)^{-1}=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(-h)^i$ since $H^N=0$. Thus $q$ is a unit. Consequently every proper ideal lies in $J_Q$ and $Q$ is local with exactly that maximal ideal. Steps 1 and 6 give Noetherianity and completeness, proving the last clause.

source.place: Tag 0DYV and algebra.tex Tag 0DYC; elementary unit lifting through the nilpotent reduction kernel.
